lesson_title: Taxi, Crate and Lift: Newton's Three Laws
hook_text: The taxi brakes. You fly forward. Except — nothing pushed you. Nothing at all.
clip_script: The taxi brakes hard and you lunge at the seat in front. What pushed you forward? Nothing. Your body just carried on at the speed it already had — the TAXI is the thing that changed. That stubbornness is called inertia, and it is law one. Law two: only the leftover push counts. Pull a crate with 120 newtons, friction claws back 45, the crate feels 75. Share it over 25 kilograms: 3 metres per second squared. And the magic words "constant velocity" mean the leftover is ZERO. Law three: push a wall and the wall pushes you back exactly as hard — on smooth tiles you slide backwards, try it. But equal pushes land on DIFFERENT objects, so they never cancel. Now step on a scale in a lift. Lift accelerates up: 678 newtons. Down: 498. Cable snaps: zero — floating like an astronaut. Your true weight through all of it? 588. Never moved. Three laws: things carry on, leftover push over mass, and every push comes back — on someone else.
visual_style: Interior of a minibus taxi with a phone sliding off a seat at the brake moment; then a crate with force arrows shrinking to a single leftover arrow; a lift scale needle swinging 678-588-498-0 as the floor indicator moves.
mood: Punchy and revelatory — everyday moments exposed as physics.
pacing: Hard hook, three quick beats for three laws, slow satisfying finish on the lift needle.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never confuse mass with weight again.
